messages:
Maya: Hey team — hitting a pretty bad issue with streaming responses. When our mobile app switches networks (wifi->cell or toggling airplane mode), the stream cuts out mid-response and the client only shows a partial sentence. Not getting an error, just silence. This is happening on our iOS app (WKWebView EventSource) and Android (OkHttp SSE).

Priya (support): Sorry you're seeing that, Maya. Can you share a sample request ID / trace id from one of the affected sessions? Also which Redwood model + API route are you using?

Maya: Sure — saw this one earlier: x-request-id=req_8f3b2a9e, model=redwood/rt-medium, endpoint=/v1/stream. Happened after toggling wifi off. Happens ~60-70% of the time when network flaps. No 4xx/5xx in response; client just stops receiving events.

SupportBot: New internal ticket created: TICKET-4762. Assigned to @Priya (support).

Priya (support): Thanks. I'm going to gather some repro steps. A few quick asks: 1) can you capture a HAR or network trace from the client when this happens? 2) do you see any corresponding server-side logs for req_8f3b2a9e (I can ask eng to look if you don't have them). 3) what client libraries are you using (EventSource, custom SSE, fetch keepalive)?

Maya: We use native EventSource polyfill on iOS (WKWebView) and OkHttp SSE on Android. I can produce a HAR from Chrome WebView reproduce locally. I do not have server logs. I can share a minimal repro app.

Sven (eng-runtime): Head's up — tagging eng-runtime. Common failure modes: mobile NAT rebinds/TCP resets cause the SSE connection to drop. Server may still be generating tokens but can't flush because the TCP connection is dead; depending on how the client reconnects, the conversation may not resume. Do you have any client-side reconnect logic using Last-Event-ID or a conversation resume token?

Maya: No resume logic. We just reconnect and re-open a new stream. We rely on the client to show partial output and then re-request the rest, but that causes duplication or loss.

Evan (sre): Also to add — intermediate proxies (carrier-level) sometimes aggressively kill long-lived connections. If the client doesn't send any keepalive, some carriers will drop after 30s. Do you see the disconnect happen at a consistent time after idle?

Maya: Not really — sometimes immediate on network change, sometimes after ~20s idle.

Priya (support): Repro checklist I'm going to run with you: 1) capture client-side network trace (HAR or tcpdump) immediately after toggling network, 2) enable debug logging for SSE and save stderr logs from the mobile app, 3) if possible include the exact request headers (x-request-id, Last-Event-ID if present, user-agent), 4) confirm whether the client receives an empty chunk or connection close. Can you do those?

Maya: Yes. I'll attach a HAR and the client log. Quick snippet showing we call:

```js
const es = new EventSource('/v1/stream?conversation_id=conv_123', { withCredentials: true });
es.onmessage = (e) => { renderChunk(e.data); };
es.onerror = () => { /* we just try to re-open */ setTimeout(() => new EventSource('/v1/stream?conversation_id=conv_123'), 1000); };
```

Maya: When reconnecting we don't set Last-Event-ID, we only re-open and start a fresh query.

Sven (eng-runtime): That explains a lot. Streaming resumes without Last-Event-ID can't dedupe or resume partial tokens. Two parallel things we can do: short-term mitigations (client-side) and longer-term server-side improvements. Short-term recommendations: 1) Implement Last-Event-ID support on client — have the server emit an incremental event id per chunk/token, then the client reconnects with Last-Event-ID to resume. 2) Add a lightweight application heartbeat in the stream every ~15s so carriers/proxies see activity. 3) On reconnect, re-open with conversation_id and a resume_token if you persist tokens client-side.

Evan (sre): On infra side, we'll check for abrupt connection terminations for req_8f3b2a9e in ingress logs and the runtime. If the TCP FIN/RST is seen, we should correlate with any queued tokens. Also need to know if the runtime buffers tokens and flushes only on ack — some of our older runtime paths assume a live TCP stream and can drop buffer on connection reset.

Priya (support): Maya — attaching instructions for enabling debugging on iOS/Android and how to capture a pcap: 1) iOS: use Charles proxy with device -> mac, enable SSL proxying, reproduce toggle, save session. 2) Android: use tcpdump on device or mitmproxy. Please upload to the ticket.

Maya: Uploaded HAR and a client-side log snippet. Log shows:

```
[2024-12-03T15:42:11.321Z] SSE connected (conv_123) x-request-id=req_8f3b2a9e
[2024-12-03T15:42:28.012Z] network change: wifi->cellular
[2024-12-03T15:42:28.108Z] eventsource error: readyState=0
[2024-12-03T15:42:28.110Z] stopped receiving data; last event id=ev_441
[2024-12-03T15:42:28.112Z] client reopened stream (no Last-Event-ID)
```

Maya: The UI shows the last partial token: "...and then the system will" and then nothing. The server did not send an EOF or error.

Sven (eng-runtime): Thanks — that's clear. Can eng-runtime team pull the runtime trace for req_8f3b2a9e? Look for: a) TCP close events proxied by ingress, b) any flush failures in the token encoder, c) whether the runtime attempted to persist partial output to a short-lived resume buffer. If we can confirm the runtime dropped the session without persisting the last event id, then the client will have no way to resume.

Evan (sre): I'm on it — will grep LB/nginx/grpc-proxy logs for req_8f3b2a9e and correlate with backend connection RST. Also check any 502/504 from upstream.

SupportBot: @Sven (eng-runtime) and @Evan (sre) added to TICKET-4762.

Sven (eng-runtime): Quick engineering notes / repro attempt I did locally: used a curl SSE stream and killed the client TCP connection — server runtime logs show token generation continued for ~200ms after the TCP reset but then the runtime returned an error 'write: broken pipe' and stopped. No resume metadata was recorded. I also tried reconnecting with a Last-Event-ID header — our current stream handler returns 400 for Last-Event-ID when used with that endpoint (we didn't implement resume for this legacy SSE path). So two work items: 1) Add Last-Event-ID resume semantics to streaming endpoint; 2) add per-stream ephemeral buffer + event ids so clients can resume within a small window.

Priya (support): Can you estimate complexity and ETA for those two items? Customer is hitting production.

Sven (eng-runtime): Short-term patch (server): implement emitting event ids per chunk + accept Last-Event-ID to skip already-sent chunks — low to medium effort, a few days to get a safe rollback. Medium-term: implement resume token persisted in Redis and server-side resume behavior for outstanding partial prompts — medium effort, ~2-3 sprints including non-regression tests. Also need changes in console/SDK docs to show how to use Last-Event-ID.

Maya: For us, short-term is fine — if we can avoid losing user messages and get deterministic resume behavior that's critical. We'll implement client-side Last-Event-ID reconnection right away if API supports it.

Evan (sre): Operational immediate mitigation: we can enable connection-proxy keepalives and lower idle-timeouts at the LB level for affected customers (configurable per dedicated pool). That may reduce the frequency of disconnects for a week or two while eng works on resume. Priya — can you ask customer if they'd like us to enable a longer keepalive on their dedicated pool?

Priya (support): @Maya — would you like us to toggle the keepalive at the LB for your account? It may help temporary reliability at the cost of slightly higher resource use.

Maya: Yes please, that sounds good. Also planning to implement client-side Last-Event-ID logic this afternoon. Can you let me know when the server patch is available so we can test?

Sven (eng-runtime): I'll fork a small PR for emitting incremental event ids and a compatibility flag in the endpoint. I'll mark it as a feature flag so we can toggle for Maya's account first. ETA: PR tomorrow, rollout to staging in 48h, can enable on their account in canary same day.

Priya (support): Great. I'll update the ticket and schedule a quick test window with Maya once staging is ready. In the meantime, Maya — please attach final HAR + client logs to the ticket and confirm device OS versions.

Maya: Done. iOS 16.5 and Android 13. Thanks everyone. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :pray:

SupportBot: TICKET-4762 status: triaged -> in-progress.

Sven (eng-runtime): Follow-ups for eng runtime: 1) implement event-id header and accept Last-Event-ID on SSE path, 2) add short TTL resume buffer to persist last ~2s of tokens per stream, 3) add integration test that simulates TCP reset and reconnect with Last-Event-ID. Evan, can you verify LB keepalive change doesn't conflict with other customers?

Evan (sre): Will do. I'll also monitor error spikes and token-generation-continue-after-reset metrics.

Priya (support): Closing loop: will post back here once the staging patch is live and canary is enabled for Maya's tenant. If anyone reproduces the exact symptom in other customers please add to the ticket so we can prioritize.

Maya: Thanks again — will test immediately when you tell me it's ready.

[thread archived after resolution steps added and canary planned]
